claims.text: Rapid quenching produces a dual-phase FeCoNiTi microstructure containing an fcc matrix and C14 Laves precipitates.
The fcc matrix in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
The C14 Laves phase substantially enhances the coercivity of the FeCoNiTi alloy.
The coercivity enhancement does not arise from enhancement of the intrinsic orbital moment of the fcc phase.
Strong antiferromagnetic coupling occurs across the interface between the Ti-rich C14 phase and the Fe/Co-rich fcc phase.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling creates a local magnetic dead layer.
The magnetic dead layer suppresses the local net saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
The fcc/C14 phase boundary pins domain walls and creates a high-energy barrier to domain-wall motion.
Hybridization between Ti 3d states in the C14 phase and Fe/Co 3d states in the fcc phase mediates the interfacial magnetic behavior.
Lattice mismatch between the fcc and C14 phases produces strain-induced magnetic anisotropy.
Interfacial pinning and strain-induced anisotropy together overcome the coercivity limitation associated with low orbital moments in the fcc phase.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy will exhibit a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
A single-phase fcc FeCoNi control alloy will have coercivity below 100 Oe at 400 K.
A C14-dominant alloy will exhibit a distinct lower-temperature magnetic transition attributable to the C14 phase.
A C14-dominant alloy will have lower overall saturation magnetization than the fcc phase alone.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys are capped at 100 Oe coercivity because they have insufficient orbital moments and lack strong pinning centers.
The proposed mechanism requires a thermodynamically stable C14 phase forming coherent or semi-coherent interfaces with the fcc matrix.
Spin-polarized DFT on an explicit fcc/C14 interface supercell can test the interfacial spin-resolved density of states and the sign of exchange coupling.
Increasing C14 volume fraction should increase coercivity if interfacial C14 pinning is the operative mechanism.
Ferromagnetic interfacial coupling or coercivity remaining below 150 Oe at 400 K despite the C14 phase would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism assert strong antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling, while the uncertainty field states that even the sign of the coupling—ferromagnetic versus antiferromagnetic—is not definitively known.
